limitations: Missing localisation annotations do not establish biological absence from a compartment.
Matching gene symbols and taxonomy resolve candidate counterparts, not independently verified orthology; renamed genes and one-to-many orthologues need an orthology resource.
Comparisons use exact location IDs (or unambiguous normalized labels when IDs are missing), without ontology ancestor expansion. Broad and specific membrane terms need not conflict.
Annotations may concern different tissues, conditions or isoforms. Their overlap does not establish identical localisation, and annotation differences do not establish biological differences.
UniProt annotations alone do not establish a drug mechanism or drug safety; additional comparative literature and experimental evidence are required.

source_records.source: CELLxGENE Discover gene expression, Homo sapiens GAPDH (ENSG00000111640), healthy tissue, snapshot 1762972271

limitations: Mouse orthologue unresolved: Ensembl HTTP 500 resolving GAPDH to mus_musculus.
Detection fraction is the share of cells with at least one read for the gene; RNA detection is not protein abundance, and a zero is a technical non-detection, not biological absence.
CELLxGENE Discover aggregates many datasets per tissue and cell type; dataset IDs, assays and donors behind each aggregate are not itemised by this API.
Matched populations share exact Cell Ontology and UBERON IDs, but annotation practice differs between human and animal studies, so equivalent labels need not be equivalent cells.
Values from independent experiments are descriptive only; no normalised cross-species fold change is computed.
Genes with many pseudogenes or paralogues (e.g. mouse Gapdh) lose multi-mapping reads during alignment, which lowers detection for technical reasons in whole datasets.

limitations: Animal tissue expression unavailable: EnsemblAPIError: Ensembl HTTP 500 resolving GAPDH to mus_musculus.
GTEx TPM and Bgee expression scores come from different methods and scales; they are shown side by side and must not be divided or ranked against each other.
Bgee is queried for present (expressed) calls; a tissue without a call has no evidence either way, which is not evidence of absence.
Organ-level matches compare a GTEx sub-site with a whole-organ animal term, so regional differences can be hidden.
GTEx samples are post-mortem adult tissue; Bgee aggregates heterogeneous studies, stages and strains, so conditions are not matched.
